newsitem.title: UK: UK Foreign Secretary sees EU deal at Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: UK Foreign Secretary sees EU deal at Amsterdam.

text.p: New British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Friday after talks with visiting Dutch premier Wim Kok that he believed the European Union would be able to conclude a treaty in Amsterdam next month to overhaul the 15-nation bloc.

But Kok told reporters that all EU governments would have to make compromises. "Without compromises ... there will be no treaty of Amsterdam," he said after meeting Cook and Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair.
Cook said he and Blair had received a good, positive response from Kok to their demand that Britain be allowed to retain control over its borders as part of any new treaty.

He said the fact that Kok had sought a meeting within a week of Labour taking office showed that Britain was now being taken seriously once more in Europe after the hostility shown by the previous Conservative government.

"I now believe that it will be possible for us to reach an agreement in Amsterdam and we have told the presidency that it will be our intention to come to Amsterdam to reach an agreement provided that we are satisfied that British national interests have been served," Cook said.

Kok said problematic issues in the way of a treaty deal next month included the EU's role in formulating foreign policy, home and justice affairs and whether a vanguard of member states should be allowed to forge ahead in particular areas without other members.
